sources.entry: gTTS - Python library and CLI tool for converting text to speech using Google Translate TTS.

summary.one_liner: gTTS is a Python library and command-line tool that converts text to spoken MP3 audio using Google Translate's text-to-speech functionality.
summary.what_it_does: It takes input text and generates speech as mp3 data, which can be written to a file, returned as a file-like object or bytestring for further audio processing, or sent to stdout. It includes a speech-specific sentence tokenizer intended to handle long text while keeping intonation, abbreviations, and decimals intact. Text pre-processors can be customized, for example to provide pronunciation corrections. It is usable both from Python (gTTS class with a save method) and from the shell via the gtts-cli command.
use_cases: convert text to speech in Python scripts
generate mp3 narration from text files
create spoken audio from the command line
add voice output to a project
produce audio for further manipulation in memory
notable: Usable as both a Python library and a CLI tool (gtts-cli)
Output to file, file-like bytestring object, or stdout
Speech-specific sentence tokenizer for unlimited text length
Customizable text pre-processors for pronunciation corrections
caveats: Not affiliated with Google or Google Cloud; relies on the undocumented Google Translate speech functionality
Breaking upstream changes can occur without notice
Different from Google Cloud Text-to-Speech, so not a substitute for that paid service
